paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
Batteries, electromagnets, relays, Morse telegraph, line codes, copper/iron wires, submarine cable, telephone transmitters and switchboards.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: Railway operators, Western Union, Bell-system predecessors, cable companies, national postal and telegraph administrations. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Telegraph circuit endpoints and relay stations; later human-operated telephone exchanges and long-distance trunks.
Per-message tariffs, telephone subscriptions, cable concessions, leased circuits and financial quotation services.
Telegraph messages were encoded into electrical pulses and reconstructed; telephone circuits conveyed continuously varying speech signals.
A stock-price quotation transmitted by telegraph could arrive faster than a physical courier. Telegraph operators encoded characters as timed signals; the receiver decoded them into written text.
Line rights-of-way, international cable landing permissions and tariff regulation made communications a political-economic infrastructure, not merely a device invention.
